//: Why this file exists: VS Code exposes no native 'a skill was invoked' signal, so we observe it indirectly. We register
a PostToolUse hook that the host runs after every tool call; the script records when any skill is activated — a 'skill'
tool call, or a read of any skill's SKILL.md (the observable proxy for 'a skill was activated'). There is no allowlist:
any skill counts. Tracking is scoped to C# Dev Kit purely by extension activation — the host only loads this plugin when
the 'csdevkit.dotnetSkillsEnabled' context is set, and that context is set exclusively during extension activation (see
the chatPlugins 'when' clause in package.json). The skill-survey service later reads those records to decide whether
to show the feedback survey. A plugin hook is the only way to register a PostToolUse callback in the host, which is why
This is the Open Plugin host's auto-loaded hook-config location ('hooks/hooks.json'), so the hook loads without the
manifest needing to point at it. The 'bash'/'powershell' keys and the '${PLUGIN_ROOT}' token are the Open Plugin host's
cross-platform hook dialect; '${PLUGIN_ROOT}' is expanded only because '.plugin/plugin.json' selects the Open Plugin format.
Precedent: microsoft/GitHub-Copilot-for-Azure uses an identical PostToolUse + bash/powershell + ${PLUGIN_ROOT} hook
(plugin/hooks/copilot-hooks.json) to run its own telemetry-tracking script.
